India Must Build Resilient Supply Chains to Lead the Global Energy Transition: HD Kumaraswamy
articles.full_content:
Green Steel, Advanced Manufacturing Key to India's Energy Security Vision: HD Kumaraswamy Energy Security Today is Defined by Manufacturing Capability, Not Just Resources: HD Kumaraswamy India Must Become a Global Producer of Clean Energy Technologies: HD Kumaraswamy at CII Energy Conference Steel, Supply Chains and Self-Reliance to Drive India's Clean Energy Future: HD Kumaraswamy
Union Minister for Steel and Heavy Industries H.D. Kumaraswamy on Thursday asserted that the definition of energy security has undergone a fundamental transformation, stating that in today's rapidly evolving global landscape, a nation's strength is determined not merely by access to energy resources but by its ability to manufacture, innovate and build resilient supply chains for the technologies that will power the future.
Delivering the keynote address at the Special Plenary Session on "Energy Security & Supply Chains" during the 7th CII International Energy Conference & Exhibition in New Delhi, the Minister outlined India's strategy to emerge as a global manufacturing hub for clean energy technologies under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, emphasising that industrial capability and energy security are now inseparable.
"Today, under the visionary leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India's energy security is no longer defined solely by access to energy resources. It is increasingly determined by our ability to manufacture, innovate and build resilient supply chains for the technologies that will power the future," the Minister said.
He noted that recent geopolitical developments, supply chain disruptions and growing competition for critical minerals have reshaped global industrial priorities, making manufacturing resilience and technological capability central to national economic security.
Kumaraswamy said India is responding to these global shifts through the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, building globally competitive domestic manufacturing capabilities while remaining deeply integrated with trusted international value chains.
"India should not merely become one of the world's largest consumers of clean energy technologies. India must become one of the world's leading producers of the equipment, materials and technologies that will drive the global energy transition," he said.
Highlighting the role of the Ministry of Steel and the Ministry of Heavy Industries in this transformation, the Minister said that the country's energy ambitions would be realised only through a strong manufacturing ecosystem encompassing steel, heavy engineering, batteries, transformers, power equipment, electric mobility, construction equipment and advanced industrial technologies.
Describing steel as the backbone of the clean energy transition, Kumaraswamy said every major investment in renewable energy infrastructure, from solar parks and wind turbines to transmission networks, battery manufacturing facilities, ports and green hydrogen projects depends fund

Initiatives adopted for Quality Drinking Water Supply under Jal Jeevan Mission
articles.full_content:
The Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) – Har Ghar Jal, was launched in August 2019, in partnership with States/ UTs to make provision for potable tap water supply in adequate quantity, of prescribed quality and on regular & long-term basis to rural households. Under JJM, as per existing guidelines, Bureau of Indian Standards’ BIS:10500 standards are adopted as benchmark for quality of water being supplied through the piped water supply schemes.
At the start of the Mission, only 3.24 crore (16.72%) rural households were reported to have tap water connection in the country. As on 18.07.2026, out of 19.36 crore rural households, around 15.89 crore (82.09%) rural households have been provided tap water connection.
Under JJM, while planning water supply schemes to provide tap water supply to households, priority is given to habitations affected by chemical contaminants. States/ UTs have been advised to plan and implement piped water supply schemes based on alternative safe water sources/ bulk water transfer for the villages with water quality issues. Moreover, any water supply scheme undertaken under JJM is approved after the recommendation of Source Finding Committee of the respective State Government, to the effect that the identified water source planned under the scheme, has sufficient yield for sustaining water supply as per required norm.
Drinking Water being a State subject, the responsibility of Planning, Designing, Approval, Implementation, Operation & Maintenance of drinking water supply schemes, including those under the Jal Jeevan Mission, is vested with State/UT Governments. The Government of India supplements the efforts of the States by providing financial, policy guidance and technical assistance .
In consultation with various stakeholders 'Concise Handbook for Monitoring Water Quality of Piped Drinking Water Supply to Rural Households’ was released in December 2024 for guidance to States/UTs. This handbook recommended for a comprehensive testing of drinking water samples at various testing points such as source, treatment plant, storage and distribution points, and remedial action wherever necessary, to ensure that the water supplied to households is of prescribed quality (BIS:10500). The recommended remedial actions include the immediate closure of chemically contaminated water sources, notifying the result to the relevant authorities and affected communities, providing safe drinking water as per JJM guidelines (at least 8-10 lpcd) through a safe source or through alternate means immediately within 24 hrs till piped water supply is restored, implementing emergency treatment measures, actions such as cleaning of OHTs, check pipe line leakage, etc. within 7 days, testing all basic and area-specific chemical as well as bacteriological parameters, and, if found safe, restore water supply from a safe source in case of chemical contaminants. As per the bio-monitoring conducted during 2024-25 at 50 locations along River Ganga and its tributaries and 26 locations along River Yamuna and its tributaries, the biological water quality (BWQ) predominantly ranged from ‘Good’ to ‘Moderate’. The presence of diverse benthic macro-invertebrate species indicates the ecological potential of the rivers to sustain aquatic life.
Under the Namami Gange Programme, biodiversity conservation has been integrated as a key component of river rejuvenation through scientific research, habitat restoration, species recovery, fisheries conservation, wetland restoration and afforestation.
Under the Namami Gange Programme, biodiversity conservation has been taken up through scientific assessment, habitat restoration, species recovery and community participation. Scientific surveys covering about 7,680 km of river stretches have documented 3,037 gharials leading to preparation of the National Gharial Conservation Action Plan. The National Centre for River Research has been established at the Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun, and four Aquatic Animal Rescue and Rehabilitation Centres, along with India's first Dolphin Rescue Ambulance, have strengthened rescue, rehabilitation and monitoring of aquatic fauna, and rehabilitation of Gangetic Dolphins, turtles and other aquatic fauna. Around 6,800 aquatic animals have been rescued and rehabilitated under the programme. Through conservation breeding programmes, more than 1,500 freshwater turtle hatchlings have been produced, 711 turtles have been released into the River Ganga, while 893 gharial yearlings and 1,899 turtles have been released into their natural habitats. NMCG is also supporting the release and post-release monitoring of the Critically Endangered Red-crowned Roofed Turtle (Batagur kachuga) through the Turtle Survival Alliance Foundation India (TSAFI).
Scientific assessments have documented 215 fish species (206 native and 9 exotic) in the River Ganga. In collaboration with the ICAR–Central Inland Fisheries Research Institute (CIFRI), NMCG has undertaken scientific river ranching for restoration of native fish populations. About 2.05 crore fish seeds, comprising Indian Major Carps, Mahseer and Hilsa, have been ranched in the Ganga and its tributaries. The Union Cabinet, chaired by Hon'ble Prime Minister, approved Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 on 10 th March 2026 , extending the Mission till December 2028 with an enhanced focus on ensuring reliable, adequate and safe drinking water services for every rural household. The Mission has been approved with a total outlay of ₹8.69 lakh crore , including Central assistance of ₹3.59 lakh crore , to support States and UTs in achieving universal and sustainable drinking water coverage.
To ensure that progress under the Mission remained uninterrupted, during the transition period, from the completion of the earlier JJM 1.0 Mission to the approval of JJM 2.0, several States continued implementation of approved rural water supply schemes using their own financial resources. Recognizing these efforts and to maintain implementation momentum, the Government of India has reimbursed ₹5,289.09 crore as Central share to 10 States in the FY 2026-27. A major reform introduced under JJM 2.0 is the Scheme-based Payment and Release through SNA SPARSH platform that enables scheme-level fund release, expenditure tracking and real-time monitoring of financial progress. SNA SPARSH facilitates payments linked to individual water supply schemes, thereby improving accountability, transparency, auditability and efficiency in utilisation of public funds.

GOBARdhan: Fuelling Clean Energy and Rural Growth
articles.full_content:
GOBARdhan: Turning Waste into the Engine of India's Growth
India currently meets nearly 50 per cent of its natural gas requirement through imports, making energy security a strategic priority. Recent geopolitical developments and disruptions along the Strait of Hormuz, a route that carries nearly 55 to 60 per cent of India's Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) imports, have underscored the importance of strengthening domestic energy production. In this context, the Union Cabinet approved GOBARdhan, the National Circular Bioenergy Scheme, with a total outlay of ₹ 23,731 crore on 06 August 2026 .
Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan (GOBARdhan) was originally launched under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) in 2018 as an integral component of Solid and Liquid Waste Management (SWM), converting bio-waste - animal waste, kitchen leftovers, crop residue and market waste, into biogas and bio-slurry, thereby ensuring cleanliness in villages and improving rural lives.
Earlier, the Compressed Biogas (CBG) ecosystem was spread across four different ministries. To ensure better coordination and accelerate the sector's growth, the Government has consolidated the entire scheme under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. This reform enables a unified approach to policy, implementation and sectoral development.
The Scheme will be implemented from FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36 and will establish Compressed Biogas as a major pillar of India's future energy mix.
Through assured demand, remunerative and stable pricing, capital assistance, pipeline infrastructure, credit guarantee and technology development, GOBARdhan will be providing the strong framework to scale up India's CBG sector nationwide.
· To increase nearly ten-fold domestic CBG production
· mobilize large-scale private investment
· create a vibrant circular bioeconomy across the country.
Nodal Ministry : Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG)
Implementation Period : FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36
Total Outlay : ₹23,731 crore
· India's waste will fuel India's growth.
· India's villages will become centres of clean energy production.
· India's farmers will become partners in the nation's energy security.
From a Strong Foundation to National Scale
Over the past several years, the Government of India has systematically built the foundations of the CBG sector through:
· Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT) initiative
· Market Development Assistance (MDA) Scheme for organic manure
· Biomass Aggregation Machinery (BAM) Scheme
· Development of Pipeline Infrastructure (DPI) Scheme
• Central Financial Assistance (CFA) for CBG plants under the National Bioenergy Programme
The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG) is implementing the Biomass Aggregation Machinery (BAM) Scheme to support Compressed Biogas producers in procuring biomass aggregation equipment. No concession or commitment on import of Ethanol for fuel blending from the United States
articles.full_content:
Recent claims in the media suggesting that India is importing and intends to import large quantities of ethanol from the United States (U.S.) for fuel blending are baseless and factually incorrect. As per the domestic policy framework, ethanol used for fuel blending under the Ethanol Blended with Petrol Programme is sourced entirely from domestic producers. There is no import of ethanol for fuel blending from the U.S.
Further, no concessions or commitments relating to the import of ethanol for fuel blending from the U.S. have been made in the India-U.S. Trade discussions. Accordingly, any suggestion of a policy change to permit large-scale imports of fuel ethanol from the U.S. is misleading. India’s fuel blending programme and ethanol procurement continues to be governed solely by India’s domestic policy requirements.
Abhishek Dayal/ Ishita Biswas

Soreng, Sikkim | 06 August 2026
The MSME-Development & Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Gangtok, under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India, in association with the District Administration, Soreng, successfully organised a PM Vishwakarma One-Day Awareness Programme on Branding and Marketing at Soreng today, 06 August 2026.
The programme aimed to strengthen the entrepreneurial capabilities of PM Vishwakarma artisans through sessions on branding, packaging, marketing, financial inclusion, Artificial Intelligence, and various schemes of the Ministry of MSME.
The programme was inaugurated by Shri Dhiraj Subhedi, District Collector, Soreng, as Chief Guest. He appreciated the Ministry of MSME’s efforts to create awareness among traditional artisans and promote entrepreneurship through the PM Vishwakarma Scheme. He urged artisans to adopt modern branding, digital technologies and institutional support to enhance the value and marketability of their products while preserving traditional craftsmanship.
The programme was also graced by Shri D. R. Bista, ADM, Soreng, Shri Ongdu Sherpa, ADC (Dev), Soreng, and Shri Roshan Sharma, MEO, Soreng, as Guests of Honour. They appreciated MSME-DFO Gangtok for bringing expert knowledge and government support services to the artisan community.
Delivering opening remarks, Shri Nirmal Chowdhury, IEDS, Assistant Director & Head of Office, MSME-DFO Gangtok, outlined the objectives of the programme and highlighted flagship schemes of the Ministry supporting enterprise development, technology upgradation, credit access, market promotion and capacity building.
Technical sessions included a presentation by Prof. P. K. Das, Assistant Professor, Sikkim University, on branding, packaging and marketing, emphasizing brand identity, packaging and digital promotion for making traditional products market-ready.
Shri Nitish Kumar, Lead District Manager, Soreng, conducted a session on PM Vishwakarma Credit Facilitation and distributed loan sanction orders to 15 artisan beneficiaries.
Shri Sukhram Rai, SLPMU, Sikkim, demonstrated AI-powered tools for catalogues, promotional content, logos and digital marketing.
Dr. Rahul Kamble, IEDS, Assistant Director, MSME-DFO Gangtok, gave an overview of Ministry of MSME schemes for entrepreneurship, credit, technology and market support.
A representative from India Post conducted a session on Export Facilitation through Dak Niryat Kendra, sensitizing artisans on export procedures and global market access.
An exhibition of products made by PM Vishwakarma artisans of Soreng district was also organized.
The programme witnessed enthusiastic participation from artisans, government officials, financial institutions, PRI members and other stakeholders.
The programme concluded with a vote of thanks by Dr. Rahul Kamble. MSME-DFO Gangtok reiterated its commitment to continue organizing such programmes across Sikkim to empower artisans and strengthen the MSME ecosystem under A

Union Environment Minister chairs Parliamentary Consultative Committee Meeting of Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change in New Delhi
articles.full_content:
Committee deliberates on Strengthening Human–Wildlife Conflict Mitigation through Technology, Community Participation and Coordinated National Action
The Parliamentary Consultative Committee of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change met today in New Delhi, under the Chairmanship of the Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav. The agenda of the meeting was to deliberate on the issue of Human–Wildlife Conflict (HWC) and the measures required for strengthening prevention, mitigation and long-term coexistence between people and wildlife. Dignitaries in attendance included Union Minister of State (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, along with Members of Parliament as part of the Committee, besides senior officers of the Ministry, PCCFs and Chief Wild Life Wardens of participating States.
The Committee was apprised of the follow-up action taken on the directions issued during its previous meeting held on 18.12.2025. These included consultations by States and Union Territories with Members of Parliament from conflict-affected areas. During the meeting, the Ministry highlighted that conflict patterns vary across landscapes, with human–elephant conflict being predominant in several States, while conflicts involving tigers, leopards, bears, rhinoceroses, wild boars, gaurs, primates and other species require location-specific management approaches.
The Committee was informed about the establishment of the Centre of Excellence on Human–Wildlife Conflict (CoE-HWC) at SACON, WII South Centre, Coimbatore, announced by the Prime Minister of India, during the 7 th National Board for Wildlife meeting. The Centre has been established as a national institution for scientific research, technological innovation, policy support, capacity building and community-centred approaches for effective management of human–wildlife conflict. The Committee also noted the launch of the National Human–Wildlife Conflict Portal on 10.07.2026, as a unified digital platform for recording conflict incidents, data management, knowledge sharing and decision support. Further, it was informed that the Regional Action Plan (RAP) on Elephant Conservation for South India has been approved.
Presentations were made by the States of Assam, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh , highlighting their conflict scenarios, mitigation measures, community participation initiatives, use of technology, institutional mechanisms and recommendations for strengthening national efforts. The experiences presented underscored the importance of landscape-specific planning, rapid response systems, habitat improvement, protection of wildlife corridors, scientific monitoring, early warning systems, community engagement and inter-State coordination.
The discussions emphasised that effective management of human–wildlife conflict requires an integrated approach combining ecological conservation with protection of human lives and livelihoods.

The agenda of the meeting was to deliberate on the issue of Human–Wildlife Conflict (HWC) and the measures required for strengthening prevention, mitigation and long-term coexistence between people and wildlife. Dignitaries in attendance included Union Minister of State (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, along with Members of Parliament as part of the Committee, besides senior officers of the Ministry, PCCFs and Chief Wild Life Wardens of participating States.

articles.full_content:
Sustainable energy infrastructure plays a vital role in promoting economic development while ensuring environmental conservation. Through timely institutional support, many entrepreneurs are contributing towards India's renewable energy transition.
One such inspiring example is Palnadu Solar Power Pvt. Ltd. , a renewable energy enterprise established by Ms. Sujatha Seelam in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh. The company's journey demonstrates the transformative impact of the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in supporting Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to build sustainable businesses.
Palnadu Solar Power Pvt. Ltd. established a 5.5 MW grid-connected solar power plant to generate clean and sustainable electricity, helping meet the growing power requirements of the region while contributing to India's renewable energy goals. Recognising the project's long-term potential, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes extended financial assistance of ₹ 15 crore in 2015 through Venture Capital (Equity with Optionally Convertible Debentures) , enabling the successful establishment and commissioning of the solar power project.
5.5 MW Grid-Connected Solar Power Plant
The financial assistance enabled the enterprise to establish a modern solar power generation facility that is successfully supplying clean energy while strengthening the company's financial position. The project has generated direct and indirect employment opportunities for local communities, established strong market linkages with clients, and contributed towards sustainable rural development through reliable renewable energy generation.
The project has emerged as a successful model of clean energy entrepreneurship by creating valuable renewable energy infrastructure and promoting environmentally sustainable development. Through reliable solar power generation, the enterprise is supporting rural power requirements while creating livelihood opportunities and contributing to India's transition towards green energy.
Reflecting on the journey, Ms. Sujatha Seelam said:
"The timely and concessional financial support received under VCF-SC enabled us to set up a 5.5 MW solar plant at Vijayawada. Today, Palnadu Solar is supporting the rural power requirement along with multiple job opportunities at the village level."
5.5 MW Grid-Connected Solar Power Plant
The success of Palnadu Solar Power Pvt. Ltd. demonstrates how targeted financial assistance under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castates (VCF-SC) is empowering Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to invest in renewable energy and sustainable infrastructure. By enabling access to concessional finance, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to promote entrepreneurship, generate employment, strengthen rural economies, and contribute to India's vision of a cleaner, greener and more sustainable future.

Strengthening Varanasi's Role as a Global Spiritual Destination Through Modern Connectivity
articles.full_content:
Varanasi, one of the world's oldest living cities and the spiritual capital of India, welcomes over 15 crore tourists and pilgrims every year. While this growing influx reflects the city's global significance, it has also placed tremendous pressure on its urban transport network. Congestion on key arterial roads often results in long travel times to major religious, educational and cultural landmarks, affecting both pilgrims and residents while impacting logistics and economic activity. To address these challenges, the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) proposed a transformative urban mobility solution, which was approved by the Union Cabinet last month. The Cabinet has approved the development of a 46.039 km six-lane Greenfield Ganga Elevated Corridor, along with ramps, loops and an extradosed Foot Over Bridge, between NH-19 and the Varanasi Ring Road (NH-135B) in Uttar Pradesh, at a total capital cost of ₹14,447.64 crore. Conceived as a high-speed, access-controlled corridor, the project will connect NH-19, the Varanasi Ring Road, Ramnagar, Banaras Hindu University (BHU) and other key destinations, significantly decongesting the road network of Varanasi and Chandauli while strengthening Varanasi's position as a global spiritual destination.
Connecting Millions to Kashi
The project is designed to make journeys to Kashi faster, safer and more convenient for millions of pilgrims and visitors. It will dramatically improve connectivity to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, the Ghats of Varanasi, Namo Ghat, Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Ramnagar Fort and Kashi Railway Station, ensuring easier access to the city's most important religious and cultural landmarks.
An elevated spur between BHU/Lanka and Samne Ghat will further ease congestion at the busy Lanka Junction by separating through traffic from local traffic movement. Together, these improvements will enhance the pilgrimage experience while reducing pressure on the existing city road network.
Designed for an operating speed of 80-100 kmph, the corridor is expected to reduce average travel time across the project influence area from nearly 60 minutes to about 20 minutes, a reduction of approximately 67 per cent. Travel time between NH-19 and Kashi Railway Station will also reduce from around 50 minutes to about 25 minutes, making travel significantly faster and more reliable for residents, pilgrims and tourists alike.
Where Heritage Meets Modern Infrastructure
Building modern infrastructure in a city with over 3,000 years of history demands an approach that respects its cultural legacy. The corridor incorporates several landmark engineering features, including an iconic 910-metre cable-stayed bridge across the River Ganga, a 1.32 km extradosed Foot Over Bridge-cum-Major Bridge equipped with travelators that will provide seamless pedestrian connectivity to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, and a Rail Over Bridge over the existing and proposed Malviya Bridge.

Good News for Container Train Operators as They Can Operate Across All Routes with a Single All India Licence, Improving Ease of Doing Business
articles.full_content:
Indian Railways Simplifies Licensing Framework; Reforms to Reduce Transportation Costs and Pollution, Ease Road Congestion and Benefit Industry, Particularly MSMEs s Other Reforms Include a Uniform Registration Fee of ₹25 Crore and No Renewal Fee for Extension
Indian Railways has approved modifications in the Model Concession Agreement (MCA) governing permission for operators to run container trains on the Indian Railways network. Under the approved changes, Container Train Operators (CTOs) will be permitted to run container trains on all routes across the network under a single All India license, with a uniform registration fee of Rs 25 crore, doing away with the earlier system of separate permissions and fees for different route categories. The changes will be notified through a Gazette Notification.
Single License for All Routes
As part of the approved modifications, the existing route-wise categorisation of licences will be discontinued. Subject to approval by the Ministry of Railways, Container Train Operators will be granted a Single All India Licence , enabling them to operate container trains across all routes on the Indian Railways network.
Uniform Registration Fee
The earlier system of charging different registration fees for different route categories has been done away with. Every applicant will now deposit a non refundable Uniform Registration fee of ₹25 crore to operate on all routes on the Indian Railways network.
No Fee on Extension
The approved amendments provide that the permission granted to a Container Train Operator may be extended for a further period of 20 years after expiry. This will be done by the Competent Authority to the same operator on application, subject to satisfactory performance. No extension fee will be charged for this extension or for any future extensions to the same operator.
Relief for Existing Operators
Operators already holding Category I licenses may continue under their existing category until their concession period ends. On renewal or extension under the new license, no fee will be charged to them.
Operators in Category II, III and IV may also continue in their existing categories until their concession period ends. For renewal or extension under the new license, they will pay ₹15 crore . This is the difference between the new fee of ₹25 crore and the ₹10 crore already paid. This amount is non refundable.
These operators may also choose to migrate early to the new license before completing their 20 year concession period. They will pay the same amount of ₹15 crore for early migration.
Benefits for Industry
The uniform registration fee and removal of extension fees are expected to reduce regulatory and compliance costs for operators while simplifying the approval process.
The simplified licensing is expected to encourage greater private participation and expansion of container train operations, leading to improved rail-based freight movement across the country. Greater use of rail for container trans

Gyalshing, Sikkim | 05 August 2026
The MSME-Development & Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Gangtok, under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, in association with the District Administration, Gyalshing, successfully organised a PM Vishwakarma One-Day Awareness Programme on Branding and Marketing at Gyalshing today, August 5, 2026. The programme aimed to enhance the entrepreneurial capabilities of PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries by equipping them with knowledge on branding, marketing, packaging, financial inclusion, export opportunities, and the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for business growth.
The programme was graced by Ms. Tripti Hangma Subba, Additional District Collector (HQ), Gyalshing, as the Chief Guest. In her address, she appreciated the efforts of the Ministry of MSME in empowering traditional artisans through capacity-building initiatives. She highlighted the importance of preserving traditional skills while embracing modern technologies and market-oriented approaches to improve the livelihoods of artisans in the region. She also encouraged the beneficiaries to take full advantage of the various interventions being implemented under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme and other Government of India initiatives.
Delivering the opening remarks, Shri Nirmal Chowdhury, IEDS, Assistant Director and Head of Office, MSME-DFO, Gangtok, welcomed the dignitaries and participants and provided a brief overview of the programme. He highlighted the objectives of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme and elaborated on various flagship schemes and initiatives of the Ministry of MSME aimed at promoting entrepreneurship, facilitating access to credit, enhancing competitiveness, supporting technology upgradation, and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for micro and small enterprises across the country.
The programme was coordinated by Dr. Rahul Kamble, IEDS, Assistant Director, MSME-DFO, Gangtok, who ensured the smooth conduct of the programme and coordinated all technical sessions and stakeholder interactions.
The technical sessions commenced with an insightful presentation by Prof. P. K. Das, Assistant Professor, Sikkim University, who delivered the keynote address on Branding and Marketing. He elaborated on the significance of building a strong brand identity, product positioning, customer engagement, packaging innovation, and digital marketing strategies. Through practical examples and interactive discussions, he encouraged artisans to transform their traditional products into competitive, market-ready brands capable of reaching wider domestic and international markets.
A dedicated session on Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Product Marketing was conducted by the State Level Project Management Unit (SLPMU) team. NITI Aayog Launches Report on “Reimagining Care: Strategies for Empowering Caregivers in Viksit Bharat@2047”
articles.full_content:
NITI Aayog today released the report titled “ Reimagining Care: Strategies for Empowering Caregivers in Viksit Bharat@2047” at NITI Aayog.
The report presents India’s caregiving ecosystem and outlines a comprehensive roadmap for building an organised, professional, accessible and future-ready system of care. It positions caregivers at the centre of the care ecosystem, recognising caregiving as a skilled, dignified and valued profession, while emphasising quality of care, professional recognition, workforce welfare, institutional support, and enabling families and communities to access reliable and affordable care. The report also underlines the growing need to develop a cadre of trained caregivers to address the current and future demand of care services in the country and also the potential opportunities for Indian caregiver professionals at the global platform.
The report was released by Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairperson, NITI Aayog, in the presence of Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog and Ms. Nidhi Chhibber, CEO, NITI Aayog, and senior officials from NITI Aayog. The launch was attended by the representatives of Central Ministries, viz., Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Ministry of External Affairs, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, National Institutes, UN agencies such as UNFPA, WHO, UNRC, World Bank, Asian Development Bank, ILO, etc., and other stakeholders providing caregiver training courses/ programs.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairperson, NITI Aayog , stated that the global demand for caregivers presents a unique opportunity to establish India as a global leader in traditional caregiving, unlock substantial economic value, create employment, strengthen recognition and social security for caregivers, as well as reinforce India's cultural and knowledge-based soft power. He emphasised that the report provides a comprehensive roadmap to strengthen institutional convergence, empower family and professional caregivers, and position India as a global hub for skilled caregiving services.
Dr R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, emphasised that Seva and Samvedana have always been at the heart of India's civilisational ethos, and caregiving reflects these timeless values. He highlighted that a robust caregiving ecosystem would strengthen social inclusion, develop a caring society, empower communities, create quality livelihoods and contribute significantly to the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 .
The report prepared Social Justice and Empowerment Division of NITI Aayog draws upon extensive stakeholder consultations, international benchmarking, surveys, and field visits and identifies opportunities to position India as a global leader in caregiving services.
